observation.visible_scene: A fixed outdoor view of a bright blue sky dominated by a large backlit cumulus cloud on the right, with the sun hidden behind it so that crepuscular rays fan out toward the upper left. A lower, shadowed cloud bank fills the bottom-left, two thin power lines run diagonally across the lower third, and a tiny bit of foliage sits at the bottom-left corner. The camera and the power lines hold a constant position relative to the frame edges throughout.
visible_changes: The summit of the right-hand cloud slowly reshapes: the tall pointed tower visible early on lowers and rounds out, and in the latter half a bright backlit gap/hole opens at its top, changing the silhouette without the cloud translating across the frame.
The fan of sun rays subtly shifts in angle and intensity as the cloud edge evolves; the leftmost ray bands fade and reposition slightly relative to the first frames.
Small wisps and the rim highlights on the lower cloud bank undergo minor, gradual morphological evolution (bright edges thinning or re-forming), with no overall left-right drift of the cloud masses.
The power lines, the bottom-left foliage, and the frame borders remain stationary, indicating the apparent motion is cloud/light evolution rather than camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the brightening gap at the cloud summit is caused by the sun's continued motion behind the cloud or by the cloud thinning is not determinable from this segment.
The cloud's state before t=0 and its continued evolution after t=2.67 s are not shown.
The exact sun position is never visible (always occluded).
uncertain_details: Any very slight camera drift is indistinguishable from the static power-line reference; treated as fixed.
The ray-pattern change is gradual and low-contrast, so individual ray repositioning is approximate.
Cloud-top change is deformation/occlusion-driven, not a translation of the whole cloud.
